title: What life is made of
question: What chemistry keeps living things running?
hook: Six common elements make up over 99% of the mass of every cell in your body.
idea: Biochemistry explains life through the molecules and chemical reactions inside and between cells.

beats.explain: Proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates and lipids are biological macromolecules, while water, metal ions and amino acids are small molecules and ions.

beats.prompt: All animals require sodium. What about plants?

choices.label: Only a small subset need it, though many grow better with it
Every plant needs it as animals do
choices.feedback: It is tempting to assume life shares its needs, but sodium is essential for only a small subset of plants.

choices.label: No plant is helped by it at all
choices.feedback: Many plants do grow better in its presence, even where it is not essential.

beats.explain: Sodium is essential for only a small subset of plants, although many others grow better in its presence.

beats.prompt: one step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Biochemists study chemical processes within living organisms.
Their findings are applied in medicine, nutrition and agriculture.
Agriculture is about soil, not living things, so biochemists have no role there.
So biochemistry only matters for medicine and nutrition.
beats.explain: In agriculture, biochemists investigate soil and fertilizers to improve crop cultivation, storage and pest control, so they do have a role there.
